elliptical-orbit-energy.alt: A satellite moves counterclockwise on a dashed elliptical orbit around a planet of mass M, which sits off-center. At the near point A the satellite is closest to the planet and its velocity arrow is long; at the far point B it is farthest and its velocity arrow is short. At both points the gravitational force from the planet points toward the planet’s center, perpendicular to the velocity, and is larger at A. A bar chart compares A and B: kinetic energy K is positive and larger at A; gravitational potential energy U is negative, more negative at A; the total energy E = K + U is negative and the same at both points.
